title: U.S. Senate · Texas

context.text: Incumbent Senator John Cornyn (R) lost the Republican primary runoff to Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, 63.8% to 36.2%, on May 26, 2026. James Talarico won the Democratic primary on March 3, 2026, defeating U.S. Representative Jasmine Crockett and Ahmad Hassan.

As of September 2026, major election forecasters (Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball, Decision Desk HQ) rated the general election a Toss-up. Talarico had raised $68.6 million and Paxton had raised $9.25 million in campaign contributions as of September 2026.

summary.text: James Talarico is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate and a Texas state representative who was first elected in 2018. A former Teach For America middle-school teacher with a Harvard education-policy degree, he has also studied at a Presbyterian seminary. He won the March 2026 Democratic primary over U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett and faces Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

background.text: Born May 17, 1989 in Round Rock, Texas; attended Round Rock ISD schools and graduated from McNeil High School in Williamson County.

Earned a bachelor's degree in government from the University of Texas at Austin and a master's degree in education policy from Harvard. He also earned a master's degree in theological studies at Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary, though as of June 2026 he had not completed the Master of Divinity there, according to Wikipedia.

In 2011 he joined Teach For America and taught sixth-grade English language arts at Rhodes Middle School in San Antonio; he then became Central Texas executive director of Reasoning Mind, a nonprofit that runs computer-based math instruction.

Was first elected to the Texas House of Representatives in 2018 at age 29, winning concurrent special and general elections for the seat vacated by Larry Gonzales, and was sworn in November 20, 2018. After redistricting he moved to House District 50, which he won in 2022 and 2024.

Has served on the House Public Education and Juvenile Justice committees and, per Wikipedia, was lead author of nearly 200 bills, 16 of which became law, including a 2021 law capping out-of-pocket insulin copays at $25 per month for state-regulated plans and Javier Ambler's Law (HB 54).

Took part in the 2021 Democratic quorum break over the Election Integrity Protection Act and returned to Texas before it ended, and was among the Democrats who broke quorum in August 2025 over mid-decade congressional redistricting, according to Wikipedia.
Announced his U.S. Senate candidacy on September 9, 2025, and won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.4% of the vote over Jasmine Crockett (46.2%) and Ahmad Hassan (1.3%).
Is a member of the Presbyterian Church (USA) and active at St. Andrew's Presbyterian Church in Austin, according to Wikipedia.

priorities.text: Proposes a "cost-of-living tax cut" that would expand the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit, restore ACA tax credits, and provide a tariff rebate, paid for by closing tax loopholes and raising taxes on wealthy individuals and large corporations.
Says he will prioritize legislation to cap campaign contributions, ban dark money groups and super PACs, and ban partisan gerrymandering.
Opposes a national school voucher program and says he will fight for universal early childhood education, including free pre-K for three- and four-year-olds.

positions.summary: Says he would pay for a cost-of-living tax cut by closing tax loopholes and making the wealthiest Americans and large corporations "pay their fair share."
positions.quote: I’ll pay for it by closing tax loopholes and making the wealthiest Americans and giant corporations pay their fair share.

positions.summary: Supports free pre-K for all three- and four-year-olds and investments in childcare for children under three.
positions.quote: I’ll fight for universal early childhood education, including free PreK for every three- and four-year-old, and strong investments in childcare for children under three to ensure childcare is affordable for low- and middle-income families.

positions.summary: Says he will fight against a national school voucher program, describing it as diverting funding from public schools to private education.
positions.quote: I'm committed to strengthening our schools and fighting back against a national voucher scam that will defund schools to subsidize private education for the wealthiest.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for repealing or rolling back the Trump Administration's tariff policies.
positions.quote: Roll back the Trump Administration’s tariff policies that are raising costs for American consumers and hurting Texas business owners

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for letting every American join Medicare and for protecting the Affordable Care Act and reversing cuts to ACA enhanced tax credits, Medicare and Medicaid.
positions.quote: Allow every American — regardless of their age — to join Medicare

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for federal legislation to codify Roe v. Wade and protect access to contraception and IVF.
positions.quote: Codify Roe v. Wade and protect access to contraception and IVF

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for universal background checks for gun sales, secure storage around children, and a higher purchase age for certain semi-automatic rifles.
positions.quote: Establish universal background checks for gun sales

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for prioritizing deportation of criminals, gang members and human traffickers while creating legalization pathways for some immigrants and banning masks for ICE agents.
positions.quote: Prioritize the deportation of criminals, gang members, and human traffickers — not our neighbors who contribute to our communities, pay taxes, and pose no threat to our safety.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for reinstating federal tax credits and loans that accelerate renewable energy development, while also streamlining permitting for energy projects.
positions.quote: Reinstate federal tax credits, loans, and other tools that diversify energy production and accelerate renewable energy development

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for raising the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour.
positions.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for stopping offensive weapons sales to the Israeli government while supporting defensive systems such as the Iron Dome.
positions.quote: Protect innocent life by stopping offensive weapons sales to the Netanyahu government while supporting defensive systems like the Iron Dome

candidates.name: Ken Paxton
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff

summary.text: Ken Paxton is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate and the Texas Attorney General since 2015. A Baylor and University of Virginia Law graduate, he practiced law and served in the Texas House (2003-2013) and Texas Senate (2013-2015) before winning statewide office. He defeated Sen. John Cornyn in the May 26, 2026 Republican runoff.

background.text: Born on Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, where his father was stationed in the U.S. Air Force; the family moved frequently and he graduated from MacArthur High School in Lawton, Oklahoma, according to Wikipedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree in psychology (1985) and an MBA (1986), both from Baylor University, and a J.D. from the University of Virginia School of Law (1991).

Worked as an attorney at Strasburger & Price and as in-house counsel for J.C. Penney, then opened his own practice in 2002 focused on estate planning, probate and real estate. Ballotpedia also lists management consulting experience and affiliations with the McKinney and Frisco chambers of commerce, Stonebriar Community Church and others.
Elected to the Texas House of Representatives (District 70) in 2002 and served from 2003 to 2013.
Won a seat in the Texas Senate in 2012 and served from 2013 until January 2015.
Elected Texas Attorney General in 2014, after winning a Republican runoff over state Rep. Dan Branch, and took office January 5, 2015. He was re-elected in 2018 (50.6% to 47%) and 2022.

A Collin County grand jury indicted him in 2015 on felony securities fraud charges (accused of selling securities without a license and without disclosing that he was being paid). In March 2024 he agreed to a pretrial intervention requiring 100 hours of community service, 15 hours of legal ethics training and about $300,000 in restitution; his attorney said it was not an admission of guilt, and the charges were dismissed in June 2025 after he completed it.

In May 2023 the Texas House adopted H.R. 2377 impeaching him, which suspended him from office. In September 2023 the Texas Senate acquitted him on all 16 articles it considered and dismissed four others.
Finished second to Sen. John Cornyn in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary (40.5% to 42.0%) and won the May 26 runoff 63.8% to 36.2% (888,196 to 503,438 votes).

priorities.text: Says he will "champion President Trump's legislative priorities, including cutting taxes, securing the border and deporting illegal aliens, ending the weaponization of government, and draining the Swamp."

Cites lawsuits as Attorney General against technology and pharmaceutical companies, including a suit against Pfizer over COVID-19 vaccine claims and national opioid-crisis settlements, as part of his record.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he will champion legislative priorities including securing the border and deporting people in the country illegally.
positions.quote: champion President Trump's legislative priorities, including cutting taxes, securing the border and deporting illegal aliens, ending the weaponization of government, and draining the Swamp

positions.summary: As a Texas state senator, voted yes on HB 2, which required abortion facilities to meet ambulatory-surgical-center standards, required admitting privileges at nearby hospitals for physicians performing abortions, and banned abortion after 20 weeks of pregnancy.

stated.summary: Campaign issues page says he will stand with President Trump to "defend the unborn."
stated.quote: He will stand with President Trump to protect our gun rights, defend the unborn

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says he will oppose what it calls a transgender movement seeking to place transgender athletes in girls' sports.
positions.quote: defeat the radical transgender movement that’s desperate to put men in girls’ sports

record.text: As Texas Attorney General, led lawsuits against companies including Pfizer over COVID-19 vaccine marketing claims and participated in national opioid-crisis settlement litigation, according to his campaign website.

As a Texas state senator, voted yes on HB 2 (requiring abortion facilities to meet ambulatory-surgical-center standards and banning abortion after 20 weeks of pregnancy), which passed the Senate 19-11 on July 12, 2013.
As a Texas state representative, voted yes on SB 14 (requiring voters to present photo identification to vote), which passed the House 101-48 on March 24, 2011.

The Texas House voted 121–23 on May 27, 2023 to adopt H.R. 2377, impeaching Paxton as attorney general on articles including bribery, abuse of office and obstruction, which suspended him from office pending trial.
The Texas Senate acquitted Paxton on all 16 articles of impeachment on September 16, 2023, and he returned to office.

candidates.researchNotes: Paxton was impeached by the Texas House in 2023 on corruption-related charges and acquitted by the Texas Senate later that year; that record is now included, sourced to the Texas Legislature's bill history for H.R. 2377, the Texas Senate, and The Texas Tribune.
